A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpookyBench research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies in v2 affect particular findings, but do not prevent matching the work across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, a six-participant human study, SNR analyses, and appendix experiments on fine-tuning, frame rates, and motion coherence.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and human results and adds semantic judging, foreground-detection experiments, training-size comparisons, and motion-boundary augmentation results.

M1.justification: The benchmark-generation procedures in Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. v2 adds a diagnostic inference adaptation: Farneback motion-boundary overlays are fed to Qwen2-VL-7B and GPT-4o (Section 4.5), whereas v1 used motion-boundary overlays for analysis and visualization.

E1.justification: The principal coverage remains the 451-video synthetic benchmark; v1's 156 Object Images and 28 Shapes are consolidated into 184 Images, rather than establishing removal of shape content. v2 adds an auxiliary foreground-presence classification task with noise-only negatives and an evaluation scenario using explicit motion-boundary inputs. These extend coverage within the existing synthetic domain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Gemini 2.5 Pro rows to v1 Table 2's comparator set. The fine-tuning study changes from Qwen2.5-VL-7B to InternVL2.5-8B and Qwen2-VL-7B. New foreground-detection comparisons evaluate VJEPA-2 and DINOv3 against chance, with an additional Qwen3-VL-8B result reported in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Fine-tuning changes from 400 videos for five epochs in v1 Appendix B to 30-epoch experiments with 100, 400, and 1,100 training videos in v2. The human FPS study changes from 60 videos, 15 per category, to 120 videos, 40 per regrouped category. v2 also adds manual and GPT-4o semantic scoring, revises CoT prompts, and introduces binary-classification protocols. Its conflicting split and training-budget descriptions leave the exact binary-classifier settings unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing fine-tuning, FPS, and motion-coherence analyses, v2 adds training-size sweeps, foreground-presence controls, motion-boundary augmentation, semantic-scoring checks, and concrete failure-response case studies. SNR-threshold analysis expands from text to images and dynamic scenes. Most earlier motion-coherence examples are retained, but the Shapes example panel is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same general mean-plus/minus reporting for benchmark, human, and SNR summaries. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented. Changed summary values and sample sizes belong to results and evaluation design.

E6.justification: v2 Table 5 newly reports 51.54% overall accuracy for Qwen2-VL-7B and 59.10% for GPT-4o with motion-boundary augmentation; these are new input conditions, not improved raw-video scores. It adds near-chance foreground-detection results, zero-accuracy training-size results, and image/dynamic-scene thresholds of 6.0/9.0 dB. Human FPS and regrouped Image summaries also change under revised samples or aggregation. The original raw-video VLM results remain 0%.

T1.justification: The four SNR definitions and the underlying exact-match accuracy calculation are retained. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and v2's explanation of the binary chance-loss baseline does not introduce a new derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain SpookyBench and the approximately 98% human versus 0% VLM recognition gap. v2 removes v1's abstract claim that training on low-spatial-SNR data causes temporal understanding to degrade faster than human perception. Its conclusion emphasizes additional evidence for the largely retained architectural explanation.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the interpretation of failure: semantic judging addresses the string-matching explanation, training-size experiments address insufficient data, and augmentation distinguishes extracting temporal cues from recognizing cues presented spatially. Appendix H attributes concrete responses to timestamp hallucination, prompt echoing, pattern collapse, and language-prior scene fabrication. These extend v1's more general architectural discussion, although the causal conclusions remain stronger than the controls alone establish.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial implementation information: LlamaFactory use, judge inputs, classifier backbones, 64-frame clips at 256×256 resolution, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, and RTX PRO 6000 hardware. It also describes generation of additional training videos and a fixed test set for the size sweep. The project access route remains unchanged. Conflicting classifier split and epoch descriptions limit reproducibility despite the added detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused positioning around common-fate perception and Tangemann et al.'s random-dot segmentation work, motion-controlled diffusion, and an ARC-AGI analogy. References for new models, Farneback flow, VLMEvalKit, and LlamaFactory are also added. The central positioning against spatial shortcuts in temporal-video benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 extensively condenses and rewrites the introduction and related work, removes the separate contribution bullets, merges related-work subsections, and renames Methods to SpookyBench. Architectural implications move from Section 3.3.3 to Section 5.1, while FPS and fine-tuning receive main-text sections. The appendix is reorganized into a separately titled supplement with contents, sections A–I, and its own references.

P2.justification: v2 relocates the main benchmark table, redraws the SNR plot with three category curves, and restructures category tables and the distribution chart. It adds classifier training curves, augmentation and training-size tables, a judging flowchart, and response panels. The supplement switches to a single-column layout with enlarged retained illustrations; v1's Shapes panel is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the paper's diagnostic support: semantic judging checks whether exact matching caused the zero scores, and motion-boundary augmentation quantifies recognition once temporal cues are exposed spatially. These address weaknesses in v1 beyond merely adding more benchmark rows. However, the new classifier reporting gives inconsistent 80/20 versus 90/10 splits and unreconciled 30-, 80-, and 100-epoch accounts. These problems limit reproducibility and confidence in the architectural interpretation, making the net improvement limited.
